title: Alignment-free hybrid bonding onto a statistical nanocapacitor carpet
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a carpet of isolated 8 nm DSA-defined nanopillar capacitors | access: transistor wafer with 40 nm landing pads | sense: standard SA | integration: wafer-to-wafer bond with no cell-level alignment | substrate: separate capacitor wafer | fab: block-copolymer DSA + ALD, high-temperature anneal before bonding}. Each pad lands on ~10 random nanocapacitors in parallel, and because each capacitor is smaller than the gap between pads, none bridges two cells; the capacitor wafer can take thermal budgets the transistors could never survive.
why: Facts 1 and 4: separates the capacitor and transistor processes, removes the cell-level overlay requirement and needs no EUV on the capacitor wafer.

title: Tri-level cells pack 24 Gb into a 16 Gb array
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): only densities JEDEC already defines may ship. Store three charge levels per cell and encode 3 bits in every 2 cells (9 states >= 8) with a two-step sense against half-level reference cells inside tRCD, so a 16 Gb-sized array ships as a standard, already-legal 24 Gb DDR5 die.
why: +50% bits per wafer with no interface change, worth about three node shrinks of cost per bit (fact 4); halved sense margin must be bought back with a higher-Cs dielectric.

title: MeRAM timing fixed with NMR-style composite write pulses
idea: Inston's voltage-controlled MeRAM stalled because precessional VCMA switching needs pulse widths exact to ~50 ps, and the anisotropy spread from cell to cell caused write errors. Borrow NMR composite pulses: a three-segment voltage sequence (90-180-90 equivalent precession angles) whose errors cancel to first order in both pulse width and anisotropy.
why: Write error rate from ~1e-3 to <1e-9 at ~fJ voltage-driven writes, making a nonvolatile ~1 fJ/bit DRAM substitute practical.

title: Allosteric strain relay: piezo pulse precesses a magnetostrictive nanomagnet
idea: Allosteric enzymes switch an active site through a distant binding event transmitted mechanically. Put an elliptical magnetostrictive FeGa nanomagnet on a US-made, CMOS-compatible AlScN piezoelectric layer. A timed voltage pulse strains the magnet and rotates its easy axis, so the magnetization precesses 180 degrees in ~0.5 ns, and a tunnel junction reads the state.
why: Non-volatile magnetic bit written by voltage at ~1 fJ instead of ~100 fJ of STT current, with no SOT heavy metals (avoiding the tungsten chokepoint) and unlimited endurance.

title: Strain-switched magnetostrictive nanomagnets written by a piezo voltage
idea: Effect walk: inverse magnetostriction (Villari effect). An elliptical 50x40 nm Co-Fe nanomagnet on an AlScN piezo layer receives a 0.2-V strain pulse that rotates its easy axis 90 degrees; releasing the strain at the precessional half-period toggles magnetization, and an MTJ reads it.
why: Capacitive strain write costs ~1 aJ-1 fJ with no current, versus ~100 fJ STT and ~10 fJ DRAM cell+bitline: >=10x lower, non-volatile so no refresh; uses Co-Fe instead of Ga- or rare-earth magnetostrictors.

title: Matryoshka concentric storage shells nested in one hole
idea: Like nesting dolls, ALD alternating TiN node shells and grounded shield shells inside one 80 nm hole, then recess each shell to a different height so its rim lands on a different tier of thin-film access transistors; each shell is an independent capacitor.
why: 10x at same cost: a 20 nm-radius, 1 um-tall shell already holds ~15 fF, so 6 nested nodes x 2 bits/node gives ~12 bits from one hole etch.

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch turns cell leakage into retention
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise + #13 Other way round: hang each storage node between two back-to-back nanoscale Esaki (band-to-band tunnel) diodes so their negative-differential-resistance curves cross at two stable node voltages. Leakage then pulls the node toward its stored value instead of away from it; the diodes are doped for ~1 pA valley current, and read/write still go through the normal access transistor. Contradiction resolved: tiny capacitor vs. no refresh.
why: Fact 3: eliminates refresh (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth) for ~1 mW/Gb holding power; Cs can shrink 3-5x because no decay margin is needed (fact 1).

title: Tier-for-litho: 64 BEOL tiers on DUV beat EUV density
idea: Bits/area = tiers / cell area. Pattern a <=400 C capacitorless cell at 4F2 with F = 45 nm on immersion DUV (no EUV), deposit 64 monolithic tiers as a blanket stack, and cut them with one 3D-NAND-style high-AR etch, reaching ~127 nm2/bit versus ~864 nm2 for 6F2 at 12 nm.
why: Removes EUV (fact 4) and much of the 55% depreciation burden. Thermal budget is what blocks monolithic stacking, and the 400 C limit is exactly what unlocks it.

title: Charge-density-wave hidden state in 1T-TaS2 flakes
idea: Jump to the picosecond timescale: a ps electrical pulse switches 1T-TaS2 into a metastable hidden CDW state with orders-of-magnitude different resistance, and a longer pulse restores it; the bit is a collective electron-lattice crystal phase.
why: Speed and energy: ps writes at fJ; no ion motion.

title: Roll-to-roll transferred monolayer MoS2 gain cell
idea: IFR: an access channel too thin to leak. Closest achievable: R2R-transfer CVD monolayer MoS2 (1.8-2 eV gap, 0.7 nm thick, ideal electrostatics) onto foil to build 2T0C gain cells where the read-transistor gate is the storage node, with off-currents below 1e-18 A.
why: Facts 3 and 2: refresh interval stretches to seconds; 2D films laminate layer by layer into printed 3D stacks.

title: Redox-molecule monolayer storage node with built-in multi-level voltages
idea: Box = {medium: electrons held in surface-tethered porphyrin/ferrocene molecules with discrete oxidation potentials | access: Si FET | sense: charge read against molecule-defined levels (2 bits per cell) | integration: monolayer grafted inside a short pillar | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: U.S.-synthesized molecules attached from solution, following the North Carolina molecular-memory lineage}. Each oxidation state releases charge at a potential fixed by chemistry, so the multi-level references calibrate themselves, and retention comes from slow electron-transfer kinetics rather than transistor leakage.
why: Density (2 bits per cell) and Fact 3: chemistry sets the levels, avoiding ECC-heavy MLC sensing, using domestic organic chemistry.

title: Na: Prussian-white nanocell stores bit as sodium electrochemical potential
idea: Each cell is a ~20 nm solid-state sodium couple of two Prussian-blue-analogue electrodes (Na, Fe, C, N) across a thin Na+ conductor; a write moves a few hundred Na+ ions, and the bit is the resulting ~0.3 V open-circuit voltage sensed on a read-transistor gate.
why: The bit is a thermodynamic potential, not a leaking charge, so electronic leakage does not erase it and refresh disappears (fact 3); all elements abundant; ion transit at ns and self-discharge are the risks.

title: Vanadium dioxide hysteresis bit parked inside its transition loop
idea: MINIFY the thermal window: hold a sputtered VO2 cell array at the midpoint of its ~5-10 K metal-insulator hysteresis with a chip thermostat; a forward current pulse through a VO2/Bi2Te3 junction Peltier-heats a 30-nm cell onto the metallic branch, and a reverse pulse Peltier-cools it back onto the insulating branch, read by resistance.
why: Static, refresh-free, non-destructive read (facts 3, 8) built with two sputter targets; local Peltier cooling strength is the weak point.

title: Zr: hafnium-free ZrO2 antiferroelectric with built-in bias as bit
idea: Sandwich pure antiferroelectric ZrO2 between electrodes of different work function (e.g., TiN and a Ti-Al alloy) so the double hysteresis loop shifts and one loop straddles zero, giving two stable zero-bias states with a large field-induced switching charge as the signal.
why: AFE endurance (>1e11-1e12) beats ferroelectric HZO and avoids scarce Hf, giving a non-volatile bit with no tall pillar (facts 1, 3); holding the imprint stable over temperature is the risk.

title: Pre-implanted cleave plane lets storage substrates be reclaimed repeatedly
idea: TRIZ #10 Prior action: build the storage array in a thin single-crystal layer transferred by hydrogen-implant ion cut onto a handle wafer that carries a second pre-implanted weak plane; at end of life or after test failure, the handle is split there, re-polished and reused 5-10 times.
why: Scarce resources: cuts Spruce Pine quartz-crucible and polysilicon demand per GB ~5x through handle reuse.

title: FD-SOI back-plane island stores bit beneath buried oxide
idea: Space-grade FD-SOI already sits on a thin buried oxide; one implant mask forms isolated doped islands in the handle wafer under each transistor, and charge injected into an island shifts the front channel threshold through the 20 nm BOX like a back gate. The BOX shields the island from front-side transient strikes and front junction leakage.
why: Capacitorless gain-type cell at ~4-6F2 with ~10x the retention of floating-body cells (facts 1, 3), on existing FD-SOI lines including U.S. capacity, for one mask.

title: Anodized-alumina 1000:1 pore capacitor forest on foundry CMOS
idea: MAGNIFY aspect ratio to ~1000:1 with a beaker: sputter Al onto finished foundry CMOS wafers, anodize it into self-ordered 20-40 nm pores, then ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside; each 250-nm landing pad catches ~30 pores so no pore-to-cell alignment is needed. Tools: an anodization bath, one ALD tool and one contact litho.
why: Cs > 5 fF per cell without plasma high-AR etch (fact 1) and with tiny capital (fact 4); turns mature-node logic into embedded DRAM.

title: Strain-held Mott latch: VO2 parked inside its hysteresis window
idea: Reverse the bias logic: a static strain from a piezoelectric underlayer holds a W-doped VO2 nanobar at the middle of its metal-insulator hysteresis, and ns current or voltage pulses flip it metallic or insulating; the electronic phase, not stored charge, holds the bit and reads as ~100x resistance contrast.
why: Refresh and endurance (fact 3): nothing leaks because the state is a thermodynamic phase, and Mott switching moves no atoms (target >1e12 cycles); risks are room-temperature hysteresis width and thermal crosstalk.

title: Lava lamp: VO2 nanodot parked inside its Mott hysteresis loop
idea: Stimulus 'lava lamp' (a heat-driven state that persists) -> a 20 nm VO2 nanodot, Cr-doped and strained to widen its thermal hysteresis to ~15 K, sits on a bias heater rail holding it mid-loop; a ~5 ns current pulse flips it metallic, a cooling pulse resets it insulating, and the ~100x resistance contrast is read nondestructively.
why: Charge-free state means no leakage refresh (fact 3) and nondestructive read (fact 8); ~4F^2 cell with no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Eliminate thermal generation leakage: wide-bandgap SiC or GaN storage junctions
idea: Eliminate silicon's thermal generation current: build the storage node and access junction in 4H-SiC or GaN (3.3-3.4 eV), where intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-8 cm-3 vs ~1e10 in Si, so junction and GIDL leakage fall by many orders of magnitude; 1990s SiC DRAM test cells already held charge for hours or more at room temperature.
why: Stretches retention from 64 ms to hours (fact 3), letting Cs drop to ~1 fF and the pillar to AR ~15 (fact 1); leans on the U.S.-strong SiC power-device supply chain; risk is SiC lithographic scaling and defect density.

title: Contactless tunneling nano-relay isolates the storage capacitor in vacuum
idea: Invert 'the access device is a leaky semiconductor junction' -> isolate the storage node with a vacuum gap. A vertical electrostatic nano-relay in the BEOL never touches: it closes from ~5 nm to ~1 nm so charge tunnels in/out, and when open the vacuum gap has no junction, GIDL or trap-assisted leakage.
why: Kills the <=13 fA leakage tail that forces refresh (fact 3): retention becomes dielectric-limited (hours), recovering 10-20% bandwidth and refresh energy; no contact means no wear, keeping endurance effectively unlimited.

title: Imprint-engineered HZO capacitor read nondestructively by small-signal capacitance
idea: Box = {medium: polarization in a deliberately imprinted HZO capacitor | access: Si FET | sense: ~100 mV small-signal capacitance read (butterfly asymmetry) | integration: 1T1C over periphery | substrate: Si | fab: asymmetric TiN/conductive-oxide electrodes set a built-in imprint}. The imprint shifts the C-V butterfly so the two polarization states differ by ~30% in capacitance at 0 V, and the read senses that difference without switching, so reads never wear the ferroelectric.
why: Fact 8 and endurance: no destructive read or restore; the ferroelectric cycles only on writes, so a write-buffering cache makes endurance a non-issue.

title: FD-SOI buried-oxide back-gate cell on a 22nm shuttle
idea: Worsen: spend the whole budget inventing a capacitor process. Flip: on a ~$100k 22FDX multi-project wafer, use an isolated per-cell back-gate under the thin buried oxide as the storage node (the BOX is a free capacitor) and read the bit as a front-gate threshold shift; 24 months covers two tapeouts and retention characterization.
why: Proves a capacitor-free, non-destructive-read cell in a US-fab logic process; U.S. manufacturability with near-zero capital.

title: Asymmetric ferroelectric capacitor read by small-signal capacitance
idea: IFR: read polarization without ever flipping it. Closest achievable: build a ferroelectric capacitor with dissimilar electrodes (e.g. TiN vs WOx) so up and down polarization produce different depletion and thus different small-signal capacitance; a tiny AC probe below the coercive field reads the bit.
why: Fact 8: removes destructive read and its ~5.9 pJ/useful-bit restore, and relieves ferroelectric endurance limits because reads never switch.

title: Swap capacitor for single deep-donor atom charge state
idea: Place one deep donor (Se or Te in Si, ~0.3 eV) per cell by deterministic single-ion implantation or hydrogen-resist STM lithography. Its neutral or ionized charge state is the bit, read by a nearby charge sensor.
why: Ultimate density, about one nm2 per bit (facts 2, 4); the deep level keeps the bit stable at room temperature, which shallow P donors cannot do.

title: Water-dissolvable transient storage cells for short-service bulk buffer memory
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: fabricate cells from the 'transient electronics' palette (Si nanomembrane transistors, MgO dielectric, Mo/Mg electrodes on a polymer handle) for 2-3-year bulk buffer memory; at end of life the boards dissolve in buffered water, leaving Si and Mo for recovery.
why: Capital and recyclability: low-temperature, low-cost process for bulk capacity; full material recovery; encapsulation life is the risk.

title: Nitrogen-cooled YBCO flux-loop memory with no helium
idea: Scarcity rule: no semiconductor in the cell and no helium (Qatar supply offline). Store the bit as a clockwise or counter-clockwise persistent current in a YBCO nanoloop at 77 K in liquid nitrogen; a current pulse through a phase-slip constriction writes it and a kinetic-inductance or nanoSQUID sensor reads it.
why: Zero static power and ps writes for LN2-immersed AI racks while avoiding the helium chokepoint; density is limited by loop inductance (~100 nm loops) and HTS junction yield.

title: Po: chips grown not made — anodic-alumina vertical racetrack forests
idea: Po: chips are grown, not made. Extracted: anodize aluminium so it self-organises into ~1e11 hexagonal pores/cm2 with no lithography, electroplate Co/Ni multilayer nanowires into them, and use each wire as a vertical racetrack where 20-50 domain walls are shifted by current pulses past a read/write junction at the pore base.
why: Pore density ~1e11/cm2 times 20-50 bits per wire is ~50x today's DRAM areal density from a cents-per-m2 electrochemical step, aiming >100x per GB. Trade-offs: serial shift latency (~10s of ns to us) and contacting every pore base.

title: Bonsai minimal fab: half-inch dry pilot lines for exotic cells
idea: A bonsai master grows a forest on a tray. Build storage-element pilot lines on half-inch wafers with sealed, shuttle-based minimal-fab tools: only a local cleanroom, dry processes and no UPW plant. Each new bit physics can then be tested for ~$5M instead of ~$500M.
why: Cuts the capital and learning time behind fact 4. A line with no UPW plant uses more than 10x less water per experiment.

title: Self-clearing segmented electrode capacitor from subsea repeater film capacitors
idea: Subsea repeaters rely on metallized-film capacitors that vaporize their thin electrode around a breakdown spot and keep working; one mask patterns a 3-5 nm top-electrode film into fusible micro-segments so a dielectric breakdown burns out only its local segment. Tolerating breakdown lets the dielectric thin by ~30%.
why: ~1.3-1.4x capacitance with no new material (fact 1) and higher yield because breakdown no longer kills a cell; nanoscale fuse energetics are the risk.

title: Crucible-free memory: laser-crystallized silicon gain cells on glass
idea: Reverse the substrate dependency: deposit amorphous silicon on glass or metal-foil panels and excimer-laser-crystallize it (1990s LTPS display process, >=1 um rules) into 2T gain cells, so the storage tier needs no Czochralski ingot, no high-purity quartz crucible and no 300 mm wafer.
why: Scarce resource (Spruce Pine quartz >80%) and capital: capacity from display-class lines priced per m2, though LTPS leakage needs ~10 ms refresh; a bulk-capacity tier strategy.

title: Bimorph stress layer self-delaminates the storage tier during recycling bake
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: insert a high-CTE metal / low-CTE nitride bimorph between the storage-capacitor tier and the CMOS logic. It is inert below the 450 C back-end budget, but a 550 C recycling bake drives mismatch strain past interface toughness so the capacitor tier (Zr, Ru, Ti) curls off as flakes.
why: Recyclability: two clean streams (silicon logic, metal-oxide storage) for cheap high-purity recovery of scarce metals.

title: K: drifting potassium ions in gate oxide as threshold memory
idea: Deliberately dope a 4-6 nm SiO2 gate layer with K+ (the classic mobile-ion contaminant) and drive the ion cloud to the top or bottom interface with +/-3 V pulses; ion position shifts the read FET threshold ~0.3-0.5 V, and heavy ions cannot tunnel away like electrons.
why: Turns a historic reliability defect into refresh-free storage (fact 3) with an abundant element and standard oxide tools; ion drift time at ns pulses and sealing against thermal drift are the risks.

title: VO2 hysteresis latch held bistable by the chip's own waste heat
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise + #36 Phase transition: dope VO2 (W/Ge) so its 5-10 K insulator-metal hysteresis loop sits at the stack's operating temperature, so each nano-VO2 cell stays insulating or metallic indefinitely while warm. Write '1' with a ns Joule pulse, reset with a piezo-strain gate pulse that shifts the loop, and read resistance non-destructively.
why: Facts 3 and 8: no refresh, non-destructive read; idle cost is heat the accelerator already makes; data are volatile at power-off like DRAM.

title: Waste-heat Seebeck read: cells report state with no applied bias
idea: Effect walk: Seebeck effect. A phase-state cell whose two states have very different thermopower (insulator ~400 uV/K vs metal ~10 uV/K, e.g. a correlated oxide) spans the natural 1-5 K vertical gradient of the BEOL stack; selecting it connects it to a high-impedance sense gate that sees ~1 mV vs ~10 uV of thermovoltage, so the read is powered by waste heat.
why: The read draws no charge from the supply, only the select and low-swing sense gate are charged, cutting read energy ~10x and avoiding destructive read (fact 8); gradient uniformity and mV-level sensing noise are the risks.

title: VO2 hysteresis islands held bistable by chip waste heat
idea: Scarcity rule: no electrical hold power; the only free resource is the chip's own heat. W-doped VO2 islands are tuned so the die's ~65 C operating point sits inside their metal-insulator hysteresis loop; a Joule pulse sets an island metallic, a piezo-strain pulse (which shifts the transition temperature) resets it insulating, and read uses the ~100x resistance contrast.
why: Turns waste heat into retention power for a 2-terminal, refresh-free, sub-ns element (fact 3, no restore periphery fact 7); demands tight die-temperature control.

title: Ferroelectric nematic liquid in nanopores: a ferroelectric that cannot fatigue
idea: Box = {medium: polar ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (RM734-class, P~6 uC/cm2) | access: Si FET | sense: polarization charge released on read | integration: 10-20 nm pores in a BEOL oxide sealed with ALD | substrate: Si | fab: vacuum capillary fill}. At 1 V across 10 nm the director rotates in ~20 ns (tau ~ viscosity/(P*E)), and because the medium is a fluid, defects and domain pinning anneal out instead of accumulating as fatigue.
why: Endurance: a self-healing liquid ferroelectric, unlike hafnia; gives a FeRAM-like cell with large switched charge in a shallow pore instead of a high-AR capacitor.

title: Time-domain sensing reads two bits per cell
idea: Time-shift the read: instead of a single voltage comparison, record how long the bitline takes to cross a threshold after charge sharing using a per-sense-amp time-to-digital counter; four charge levels map to four crossing times, storing 2 bits per capacitor.
why: Cost per bit: ~1.8x bits per cell area after margin; reuses existing capacitor process.

title: Ga2O3 ultra-wide-bandgap access transistor for hour retention
idea: Time-shift retention from 64 ms to ~1 hour by replacing the silicon access device with a 4.8 eV beta-Ga2O3 thin-film transistor, whose off-state leakage can be below 1e-21 A, while keeping a conventional stacked capacitor.
why: Refresh and leakage tail: refresh energy cut >1000x; Cs can shrink 3-5x because only sense margin matters.

title: Significance-graded cell sizes for MSB and LSB bits
idea: Time-shift by bit importance: lay out arrays with large-capacitor cells for exponent and high bits and small, unrefreshed cells for low mantissa bits of AI weights and activations, which may decay gracefully between writes.
why: Cost per bit and refresh: ~25-35% area saving and half the refresh energy for FP16/BF16 tensors with negligible accuracy loss.

title: Zettacore revived: solid-state redox monolayer multiplies capacitor charge
idea: ZettaCore's porphyrin memory died because its redox molecules needed a liquid electrolyte. Tether a ferrocene/porphyrin monolayer to the DRAM storage-node electrode and cap it with an ALD solid ion conductor (LiPON-like): Faradaic charge of 1-4 electrons per molecule adds ~10-30 uC/cm2 of pseudocapacitance on top of the dielectric charge.
why: 3-10x storage charge per area breaks the capacitor wall (Fact 1) without AR 115; shorter pillars save etch steps and collapse risk. Risk: redox kinetics must reach <10 ns.

title: Tree-resin wound sealing: self-clearing electrodes isolate leaky defects
idea: Trees seal wounds with resin, and metallized-film capacitors 'self-clear' by vaporizing the electrode around a fault. Use an ultrathin 2-3 nm TiN/Al top-electrode skin that oxidizes locally into an insulator when a leakage hotspot's current density spikes during a burn-in pulse. This disconnects only the defective spot and leaves the rest of the capacitor intact.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): removes the dielectric-defect cells, so refresh is set by the bulk population, possibly a 2x longer interval, plus a yield gain.

title: Po: memory is an old TV tube — field-emitter-addressed charge spots
idea: Po: memory is an old TV tube. Extracted: revive the Williams-Kilburn tube on-chip: a Spindt field-emitter array whose tips are each deflected over a 100x100 field writes, reads (secondary-emission contrast) and refreshes ~20 nm charge spots on an unpatterned dielectric film.
why: The storage medium is a blanket film needing no lithography; only the coarse emitter array is patterned, aiming >100x lower cost per GB. Trade-offs: vacuum packaging, us access, emitter lifetime.

title: Eliminate channel charge transport for writes: caged-ion fullerene dipole bits
idea: Eliminate pushing charge through a channel: use endohedral fullerenes (Li+@C60) whose caged ion sits off-center in one of two positions, forming a switchable molecular dipole; a crossbar field flips the ion inside its cage in ~ps, and an underlying 2D-channel transistor senses the dipole.
why: 1-nm nonvolatile bit with ps writes and no lattice fatigue (facts 1, 3, 10); risks are room-temperature stability of the off-center state and readout signal size.

title: Swap ZrO2 for cryogenic quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 storage dielectric
idea: Operate the array at 20-77 K and use SrTiO3 or KTaO3, whose permittivity climbs toward 10^3-10^4 as quantum fluctuations suppress the ferroelectric transition. A planar or AR<5:1 MIM cap then reaches 5 fF in a 12-nm-class cell footprint, aimed at cryo-cooled AI and quantum-computing racks.
why: Removes the 60-75:1 pillar etch (facts 1, 4). Planar caps cut capacitor process steps by ~50%, and leakage freeze-out also cuts refresh (fact 3). The honest cost is cooling power.

title: Po: memory lives in a freezer — quantum-paraelectric cryogenic capacitor
idea: Po: memory lives in a freezer. Extracted: run memory at 40-77 K, where quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3/KTaO3 films reach permittivity of 1,000+ and access-transistor leakage freezes out; a shallow capacitor then holds more charge than today's 70:1 pillar and retention extends to minutes.
why: Breaks the charge wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3) together for liquid-nitrogen-cooled AI racks. Thin-film permittivity loss is the risk.

title: NEMS parametron: bit as the phase of a vibrating beam
idea: IFR: a bit made of motion, free to keep if lossless. Closest achievable: a high-Q nanomechanical resonator pumped at twice its frequency oscillates in one of two degenerate phases (0 or pi); a small seed signal sets the phase (write) and phase-sensitive detection reads it, reviving Goto's 1950s parametron.
why: Facts 3 and 9: no charge to leak or hammer; one shared pump replaces per-cell refresh; near-reversible dynamics allow sub-fJ writes.

title: Adiabatic ramped access recycles bitline charge through resonant LC tanks
idea: Effect walk: adiabatic charging, where dissipation scales as (RC/T) x CV2. Make the cell-plus-bitline part of an LC tank using 3D BEOL inductors and drive wordlines and bitlines with a resonant sinusoidal clock over 5-10 ns instead of ~0.1-ns steps, returning ~90% of the bitline charge to the tank after each access.
why: Bitline charging dominates DRAM access energy (facts 5, 8, 10); ramps with T~20 RC cut dissipation ~10x at the cost of a slightly longer row cycle, with standard materials.

title: Watch-escapement multi-detent nanomechanical ratchet bits
idea: Adapt the escapement and pawl: a released 15 nm beam rests in one of four van der Waals detents along a serrated sidewall, is stepped by electrostatic pulses and read capacitively, with five sealed released layers stacked.
why: 10x at same cost: 2 bits per element x 5 deposited-and-released tiers; mechanical state needs no refresh and has no dielectric wearout.

title: Zeolite autoclave cages: trapped sodium ion hops between two sites
idea: Use hydrothermal autoclave zeolite synthesis to grow sodalite films (Na, Al, Si, O) in the cell, where each cage holds a Na+ ion in a double-well site. A field pulse shifts the caged ions to one side as a bistable dipolar polarization, and the displacement charge is read.
why: Fact 3: ion-hop barriers of ~1 eV mean minutes-to-years retention with no electronic leakage path. The elements are Earth's most abundant, and the rigid cage framework means unlimited endurance.

title: Offset-printed alpha-In2Se3 sheets: ferroelectric semiconductor channel holds the bit
idea: Like offset printing transfers ink from a blanket roller, a wafer-scale stamp transfers MBE-grown alpha-In2Se3 layers onto the logic wafer. The bit is polarization inside the semiconductor channel itself, so no separate ferroelectric gate is needed, and channel conductance reads it non-destructively.
why: Facts 1 and 8: no capacitor and no destructive read. vdW layers lack the oxygen-vacancy fatigue path, so endurance aims at 1e12+, and BEOL transfer avoids front-end capital.

title: Altermagnet tunnel junction: spin-split readout without net magnetization
idea: Effect walk: altermagnetic spin splitting. Build a tunnel junction whose free electrode is an altermagnet (CrSb or MnTe, avoiding Ru) with momentum-dependent spin-split bands, so the Neel vector produces a TMR-like resistance change; write by spin-orbit or current-induced Neel switching.
why: Combines ferromagnet-grade electrical readout with antiferromagnet immunity to fields and THz dynamics, enabling magnetic cells below 20-nm pitch without dipolar crosstalk and with abundant elements.

title: Swap EUV hole patterning for guided anodic-alumina self-ordered pores
idea: Deposit 2-3 um of aluminum over DUV-made access transistors and imprint shallow DUV-defined pits at the landing-pad positions. Anodizing then nucleates pores at the pits, which self-order into ~25 nm holes with AR above 100:1, and ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN lines them as storage capacitors.
why: Exceeds the 60-75:1 pillar AR wall (fact 1) without EUV or a high-AR plasma etch (fact 4). The wet electrochemical step costs a few dollars per wafer and uses tools from the aluminum-capacitor industry.

title: Swap EUV contact holes for block-copolymer cylinder self-assembly
idea: Coat a high-chi block copolymer (PS-b-PDMS or PS-b-P2VP) into relaxed-pitch DUV guide holes, so each guide splits into a cluster of 3-7 cylinders at ~24 nm pitch. The cylinders are then transferred into the hard mask that defines the storage-node holes.
why: Replaces 2-3 of the 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4) with a spin-coat and anneal, cutting ~20-30% of litho-driven wafer cost.

title: Optical rectenna MIM diodes: transistor-free diode-isolated storage node
idea: Optical rectennas rectify THz signals with metal-insulator-metal tunnel diodes whose work-function asymmetry gives strong rectification; isolate each storage capacitor with two back-to-back asymmetric MIIM diodes (e.g., Nb/Nb2O5/Al2O3/Pt), so the node charges only when row and column voltages exceed turn-on, enabling 4F2 crosspoint decks with no silicon transistor.
why: Facts 2 and 4: transistor-free 3D stacking where each deck is deposition plus relaxed litho, all with sputter, ALD and evaporation; diode off-current at hold must reach ~1e-18 A per cell, ~1e4 below published MIIM diodes.

title: Nacre brick-and-mortar perovskite nanosheet capacitor dielectric
idea: Copy nacre, where staggered aragonite bricks sit in a thin organic mortar. Tile exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10-type perovskite nanosheets (k ~200 at 2-3 nm) in staggered, overlapping layers bonded by a 0.3 nm Al2O3 mortar, deposited by flow-coating into the capacitor. The staggered seams force leakage paths to wander, the way shell deflects cracks.
why: Hits the k~70 target for the charge wall (fact 1): k_eff ~100-150 gives ~3x Cs per area, so AR can drop from ~70 to ~25. It also removes the Zr/Hf ALD dependence.

title: Pacemaker heartbeat: NEMS parametron stores bit as oscillation phase
idea: A biologist sees life keeping information as a rhythm, like the heart's pacemaker. Each cell is a nanomechanical resonator pumped parametrically at 2f by a shared global pump; it settles into one of two phase states (0 or pi) that encode the bit, and it couples to a read line only when selected.
why: A shared pump supplies the energy, so there is no per-cell refresh; phase does not leak away like charge (fact 3) and is immune to row hammer (fact 9). It revives Goto's 1954 parametron at NEMS scale.

title: Read ferroelectric bits by strain, never by switching
idea: Flip FeRAM's read path from electrical to mechanical: each HZO or AlScN ferroelectric capacitor sits on a piezoresistive channel; a small sub-coercive voltage makes up- and down-polarized cells expand or contract (opposite piezo sign), modulating channel resistance, so polarization is read without being switched.
why: Destructive read and fatigue (fact 8): removes the read-switch-restore cycle, cutting read energy ~5-10x and limiting wear to writes only.

title: SOI-wafer supply model: capacitor arrays shipped under transferred silicon
idea: Copy the engineered-substrate business behind SOI wafers: a specialist supplier fabricates the deep-trench/ high-k storage-capacitor array (with alignment marks) on depreciated 65-nm-class tools, then layer-transfers a thin crystalline Si film on top by Smart-Cut bonding; the DRAM fab aligns and builds access transistors and periphery in that film.
why: Fact 4 capital: moves the high-AR capacitor module out of the leading-edge DRAM fab, decouples capacitor thermal budget from transistors (allowing >900 C crystallization for higher k), and creates a U.S. supplier tier; overlay through the transferred film is the main risk.

title: Sealed charge-conserving double-island cell with no path to ground
idea: Invert 'the storage node connects to the outside through a leaky path' -> make the bit a sealed, charge-conserving pair. Two metal nano-islands share one tunnel barrier and have no other conductive path; the bit is which island holds the excess electrons (dipole up/down), flipped by a field pulse from adjacent gates and read by capacitive coupling to a sense FET.
why: Charge cannot leak off a sealed pair, so refresh disappears and endurance is unlimited (facts 1, 3) at ~10 nm cells; room-temperature retention needs sub-5 nm islands and engineered barriers.

title: Self-assembled random nanodot capacitors with post-fab address remapping
idea: Invert 'every cell must be lithographically placed, identical and good' -> accept random cells and map them. Block-copolymer self-assembly drops ~15 nm metal nanodot capacitors at random over a relaxed 40 nm crossbar; built-in self-test classifies each crossing (empty, one dot, several, retention class) and writes a remap table so the controller uses only good sites.
why: Removes critical-dimension lithography for the storage layer (EUV, fact 4) and turns variability into a mapped resource instead of yield loss; map overhead and drift are the risks.

title: GaN-on-sapphire wide-bandgap charge cell that never needs refresh
idea: Invert 'DRAM charge is volatile and must be refreshed' -> pick a semiconductor whose 3.4 eV bandgap makes thermal generation ~1e-20 of silicon's. An AlGaN/GaN access transistor with a junctionless p-GaN storage node on cheap LED-grade sapphire holds charge for days to years while storage stays pure charge with no material wear.
why: Removes refresh power and bandwidth tax (fact 3) and makes the memory effectively non-volatile with unlimited endurance; reuses U.S./allied LED and RF GaN lines instead of silicon DRAM fabs; dense enhancement-mode GaN and interface traps are the risks.

title: Nanoconfined monatomic antimony phase-change cell that cannot segregate
idea: Fill 5 nm TiN-lined pores with pure Sb by RT sputtering; confinement stabilizes the amorphous phase, and melt-quench of ~100 nm3 costs ~10 fJ. A single element cannot phase-separate, which removes the composition drift that kills Ge-Sb-Te endurance.
why: Attacks PCM's endurance failure mode at its root (no elemental migration), with fJ writes in a stackable cross-point (density).

title: Si: JEDEC AI-grade memory class admitting 1% raw cell errors
idea: Define a JEDEC grade for AI weights and KV cache in which devices may ship with up to 1% raw cell BER, the controller carries a standardized LDPC/erasure layer, and buyers get a guaranteed post-correction error rate; DRAM dies now scrapped or down-binned for weak cells, and every leaky or low-margin new cell, become sellable.
why: Raises usable supply immediately through several points of yield and gives constrained cell technologies a legal market, cutting capital and scarce-resource use per usable bit.

title: VCMA precessional MTJ write with retry loop hidden inside tWR
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): every write must finish inside DDR5's ~30 ns tWR. A voltage-controlled-magnetic-anisotropy MTJ switches by a 0.5 ns precessional pulse at ~0.5 V with near-zero current, and because its single-shot error rate is ~1e-3, the die runs write-verify-retry up to 10 times within tWR, turning a probabilistic element into a deterministic DDR write.
why: Fixed spec slack becomes the reliability budget: fJ nonvolatile writes (facts 3, 10) with negligible barrier current, so endurance is effectively unlimited.

title: Adiabatic ramped write that recovers the cell's CV2 energy
idea: A step charge through any resistor dissipates CV2/2, but a ramp of duration T >> RC dissipates only ~(RC/T)*CV2. Drive wordlines, bitlines and precharge from a resonant LC tank clock so cell writes ride a slow sinusoid and their charge returns to the tank.
why: Cuts write and precharge energy 3-10x at the same 1 V / 3 V levels, getting under the voltage floor (fact 10) without lowering voltage.

title: Resonant-tunneling-diode pinning lets all cells self-restore simultaneously
idea: Invert 'refresh means reading each row and writing it back' -> let every cell restore itself at once. Each storage node connects to a shared pulsed rail through a series pair of BEOL resonant-tunneling diodes whose N-shaped I-V gives two stable node voltages; a ~1 ns global rail pulse every few ms snaps all cells to the nearer level without sensing or row activation.
why: Eliminates refresh activations, freeing 10-20% bandwidth and most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy (fact 3), and makes refresh-based row-hammer mitigation nearly free (fact 9); risk is RTD peak-to-valley uniformity at room temperature.

title: Twin resonant-tunneling diodes form a static bit at DRAM pitch
idea: Effect walk: resonant tunneling negative differential resistance. Two stacked double-barrier RTDs (Si/SiGe or GaN/AlN) in series form a Goto pair with two stable midpoint voltages; one access transistor writes the midpoint, and holding draws only the RTD valley current.
why: Static storage without refresh (fact 3) or capacitor (fact 1) in a vertical ~6-8F2 stack; feasible only if valley current density falls to ~1 A/cm2 (pA per cell), i.e. peak-to-valley ratio >10^4 at room temperature.

title: Vertical CCD charge-packet strings replacing per-bit access transistors
idea: Store bits as charge packets in potential wells under 64 stacked gate electrodes along one vertical channel, reviving 1970s CCD memory in 3D. Packets clock to an end-of-string sense amp at ~1 ns per transfer with CTE >0.99999, and a page cache hides the shift latency.
why: With no capacitor and no access transistor per bit, both 3D-DRAM blockers (fact 2) vanish. One sense node serves 64 bits, cutting periphery share (fact 7), and each bit costs one deposited gate layer.

title: Sn: SnS in-plane ferroelectric sheet stores bit as rectification direction
idea: Use few-layer SnS (abundant Sn and S), whose ferroelectric polarization lies in the sheet plane, between two lateral electrodes; the polarization direction makes one Schottky contact lower than the other so the junction rectifies left or right, read non-destructively with a small bias.
why: Non-volatile, capacitor-free bit in a 2D sheet that can be laminated into many 3D tiers (fact 2) without vertical capacitors; switching speed and SnS air stability are open.

title: NEMS parametron storing bits as oscillation phase
idea: Revive Goto's 1950s parametron with GHz nanomechanical resonators: each cell is an AlN or SiN nanobeam pumped at twice its resonance, so it oscillates in one of two phases (0 or pi) that encode the bit. A shared pump line drives thousands of resonators, and phase is read by capacitive pickoff against a reference without destroying it.
why: Facts 3, 8, 9: no charge leakage tail, non-destructive read, no row hammer; high-Q (>1e4) resonators keep shared pump power low; density is the risk.

title: Four bits stacked in one pillar hole by depth segmentation
idea: MAGNIFY bits per etched hole 4x: form an AR-60 cylinder capacitor in an ONON-style mold, then interrupt the storage electrode with three ALD SiO2 plugs so four isolated segments sit at different depths, each reached by a ring-gate vertical-channel transistor patterned in the matching mold tier.
why: Reuses today's capacitor etch while placing 4 bits per hole, ~3x density without a 26-tier lateral 3D DRAM (fact 2); each ~1.2 fF segment needs a gain-cell or sensitive sense amp.

title: Puff-pastry laminated HfO2/ZrO2 tuned to the morphotropic boundary
idea: Laminate like puff pastry folds dough: ALD supercycles stack 0.5 nm HfO2/ZrO2 leaves whose interface strain pins the film at the tetragonal-orthorhombic morphotropic phase boundary. There, field-induced polarization rotation peaks permittivity at k~60-70 without full ferroelectric switching.
why: Fact 1 directly: k~70 is the stated alternative to AR 115. Cs rises 2-3x at the same AR, and since the film never fully switches, endurance stays effectively unlimited.

title: Read resistance states by listening to their Johnson thermal noise
idea: Effect walk: Johnson-Nyquist noise. A selected high- or low-resistance cell (e.g. 100 kOhm vs 10 MOhm) is connected unbiased to a local low-noise correlator that distinguishes the ~10x noise-voltage difference over a 20-ns window; no current is driven, so the cell is never disturbed.
why: Zero injected read energy and no read disturb: per-bit read cost becomes the amortized correlator energy, potentially ~10x below bitline-charging reads in large banks; low-power amplifiers per sense group are the hard part.

title: E-ink capsule shrunk: electrophoretic nanoparticle shuttles between nanowell electrodes
idea: Each cell is a 30-nm e-beam-defined nanowell sealed by ALD, holding one charged 5-nm Au or TiO2 nanoparticle in a low-viscosity dielectric fluid; a write pulse drives it to the top or bottom electrode (~10 ns over 15 nm at 1e8 V/m), where van der Waals adhesion holds it like E-ink pigment, and read is the capacitance change or tunneling current through the particle.
why: Non-volatile, refresh-free and immune to row-hammer charge disturb, with no material fatigue; buildable with e-beam, ALD and colloid drop-casting; nanoscale liquid sealing and particle aggregation are the risks.

title: Moire silk patterns: twist-angle-defined trap lattices as litho-free storage sites
idea: Moire fabric shows a large pattern from two fine weaves; twisting WSe2/WS2 bilayers by ~1-3 degrees creates a lattice of deep potential minima at ~8-10 nm pitch, each able to trap a hole; a 50-nm e-beam gate over a patch writes trapped-hole occupancy that shifts an underlying channel threshold, a floating-gate-like bit whose sites come from the twist, not lithography.
why: Density and litho: sub-10-nm storage sites with zero patterning, built with a twist-transfer stage, e-beam and hBN encapsulation; moire trap depths (~100-200 meV) give only ms-scale retention at room temperature unless deeper heterostructures are found.

title: Overvoltage burn turns flickering VRT cells into deterministic hard faults
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial or excessive action: variable-retention-time cells flicker between leaky and good and escape test. During in-field maintenance, hit any cell flagged even once with a controlled ~2.5-3 V stress pulse that breaks its weak dielectric down to a hard short, so the next scrub always detects it and maps it to a spare.
why: Fact 3: refresh interval can follow the normal population, not the VRT tail, roughly halving refresh energy; repair becomes deterministic.

title: Spin-wave bus reads eight nanomagnets with one multiplexed pulse
idea: Effect walk: magnon phase shift. Eight 30-nm nanomagnet bits sit along a CoFeB or garnet spin-wave waveguide, each coupled to a different resonant mode; one broadband spin-wave pulse picks up a bit-dependent phase at each frequency, and a single inductive detector demultiplexes all eight.
why: Magnons carry no charge current and one pulse reads 8-16 bits, so read energy per bit falls ~10x versus charging a bitline per bit, and it reads exactly the word needed instead of a page (fact 8).

title: Lithium-niobate domain-wall conduction gives non-destructive ferroelectric reads
idea: Invert 'ferroelectric bits must be read destructively by switching' -> read the walls, not the domains. In thin-film lithium niobate on insulator, a written nanodomain creates charged conductive domain walls between two lateral electrodes; the bit is presence or absence of wall current (on/off >1e4), read without switching polarization.
why: Non-destructive read removes the write-back half of every access (fact 8) and read fatigue; non-volatile so no refresh (fact 3); LNOI wafers come from the photonics supply chain, not silicon; write endurance and sub-30 nm wall stability are the risks.

title: Dual-bit cell stores capacitor charge and floating-body charge together
idea: Million-token AI contexts are capacity-starved, so one counter-doping implant mask isolates a floating p-pocket under each access transistor; the cell keeps one bit as capacitor charge and a second as body holes that shift threshold. Reads first sense the body bit by current at an intermediate wordline level, then charge-share the capacitor bit.
why: Up to 2x bits per cell area on existing 6F2 arrays for one mask (density, cost per bit); body/capacitor disturb coupling and two retention clocks are the risks.

title: ALD oxide quantum-well charge bucket gated by band bending
idea: Grow a 3 nm In2O3 well between Ga2O3 barriers (dEc ~ 0.9 eV) by ALD at <=300 C, under a gate and over a read channel. A gate pulse bends the bands to inject electrons thermionically, retention tau = tau0*exp(dEc/kT) gives ~0.5 s at 85 C, and stored electrons shift the read channel's threshold.
why: Retention is set by a band offset chosen by composition, not by a leakage tail (fact 3), with no capacitor (fact 1). Capacitorless and repeatable in many BEOL tiers (fact 2).

title: Solid-state Williams tube: charge puddles in an unpatterned film
idea: Invert 'each bit needs a discrete patterned capacitor' -> store charge puddles in a continuous film. A semi-insulating high-k layer (rho ~1e15 ohm-cm) lies between orthogonal row/column electrode grids with a thin rectifying MIM-diode interlayer; charge injected at a crossing stays local because lateral RC spreading takes longer than seconds, like the 1947 Williams CRT memory in solid form.
why: Deletes the HAR capacitor etch and per-cell isolation (facts 1, 4): a 4F^2 crosspoint without access transistors and several fewer critical masks.

title: Nanoimprint master replicates capacitor hole arrays without EUV
idea: MINIFY litho cost per layer: e-beam write one 20-nm-hole master, then UV-nanoimprint the storage-node hole layer wafer after wafer with a ~$2M tool; periodic hole arrays are the ideal imprint case because overlay tolerance is loose.
why: Replaces 1-2 EUV exposures on the storage node (fact 4: depreciation ~55% of wafer cost) with tooling a small team can own.

title: Photonic-crystal nanocavity bistable bits in a silicon photonics foundry
idea: MINIFY optical bistable memory from fiber loops to ~1 um3 photonic-crystal nanocavities whose carrier-plasma bistability holds a bit at tens of nW bias; designed by a small team on a photonics MPW and written/read by wavelength-multiplexed light on the same bus used for chip-to-chip optical I/O.
why: Memory sits on the optical interconnect, cutting data-movement energy (fact 5) for photonic accelerators; no capacitor or EUV.

title: Cr: Cr2O3 magnetoelectric antiferromagnet written by voltage, not current
idea: Use a thin boron-doped Cr2O3 layer whose antiferromagnetic domain is selected by a voltage pulse under a small fixed bias field (magnetoelectric E-times-H switching), read via its boundary magnetization by anomalous Hall in an adjacent film or a stacked tunnel junction.
why: Write energy is displacement current only (~fJ), non-volatile with no refresh (facts 3, 10); chromium is abundant; boron doping must lift the Néel temperature above chip temperature.

title: Advance market commitment for element-agnostic trailing-node working memory
idea: A CHIPS-funded advance market commitment buys ~1 exabyte over 5 years of byte-addressable working memory from existing >=28-nm U.S. fabs at a fixed $/GB and spec (<=100 ns, >=1e15 endurance or architectural equivalent), open to any revived storage element.
why: Guaranteed demand lets revived elements (pinned wells, T-RAM, MNOS, micro-magnetics) fill idle 200/300-mm trailing capacity now instead of waiting 3-5 years for a DRAM fab; capital intensity and U.S. share.

title: Pastry chef's caramel: spin-crossover film with room-temperature hysteresis
idea: A chef knows sugar sets differently depending on whether it was heated or cooled. Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover nanofilms have a ~30 K wide thermal hysteresis loop that straddles room temperature; a local ns heat or field pulse toggles high-spin and low-spin states, and the bit is read as a 10-20% change in dielectric constant.
why: A bistable molecular state holds without refresh (fact 3), and the molecules use cheap, earth-abundant iron instead of chokepoint materials.

title: Self-selective optical global refresh through a transparent top plate
idea: Scarcity rule: zero refresh bandwidth. A transparent ITO cell plate lets a chip-wide LED flash generate carriers in a photodiode junction at each storage node, and the node's own voltage steers the photocurrent so '1' nodes recharge toward VARY while '0' nodes drain to ground, refreshing every cell in parallel with no row cycling.
why: Removes the 10-20% refresh bandwidth loss and per-row activation energy (fact 3) and refresh-driven activations (fact 9); steering selectivity and optical access through BEOL are the risks.

title: Swap silicon storage node for 4H-SiC junction-isolated node
idea: Build the 1T1C or gain-cell storage node in 4H-SiC, whose 3.26 eV bandgap cuts junction generation leakage by >10^15 versus Si. SiC DRAM test cells in the 1990s already held data for hours to years at room temperature.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3: ~46 fJ/bit and 10-20% of bandwidth). SiC boules grow without Spruce Pine quartz crucibles, and U.S. SiC fabs (NC, NY) already exist, which helps U.S. manufacturing.

title: Nanomechanical parametron stores the bit as oscillation phase
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action + #15 Dynamics: revive Goto's 1954 parametron at nanoscale. Each cell is a high-Q nanomechanical resonator pumped at 2f by a shared wordline AC drive, ringing at f in one of two phases (0 or 180 degrees); phase is the bit, the pump continuously regenerates it, and a small injected signal picks the phase on write.
why: Facts 3 and 10: no transistor leakage tail and no refresh, plus native majority-logic in memory; pump power and density are the risks.

title: Self-rolled-up nanomembrane Swiss-roll capacitor in every cell
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells + #7 Nesting: deposit a strained TiN/ZrO2/TiN/SiN multilayer flat with no deep etch, then release a sacrificial layer so built-in strain rolls it into a 5-10-turn tube; each turn adds electrode area, and lateral rolls suit horizontal 3D DRAM tiers.
why: Facts 1, 2 and 4: ~10x area per footprint from planar deposition and release, replacing 70:1 etching; scaling roll diameter to tens of nm is the risk.

title: Light switch: snap-through buckled nanobeam as a bistable bit
idea: Stimulus 'wall light switch' (two detents, no power to hold) -> a 200 nm compressively pre-stressed TiN or SiN beam is buckled up or down over a sense electrode; an electrostatic pulse on the opposite electrode snaps it through, and the up/down position changes cell capacitance ~3x for read. Built-in stress, not charge, holds the state.
why: Zero static leakage so no refresh (fact 3); no capacitor charge wall (fact 1); stacks in BEOL tiers without a lateral transistor (fact 2); ~20 ns snap at GHz resonance.

title: Mantis-shrimp Bouligand stacking breaks dielectric leakage percolation paths
idea: Mantis shrimp clubs resist cracks with helicoidal (Bouligand) layers, each rotated a few degrees from the last. Build the capacitor dielectric from 4-6 sub-1 nm crystalline sublayers separated by one-monolayer nucleation-reset films. Each sublayer then re-nucleates with randomised grain orientation, so grain boundaries never line up into straight through-paths.
why: Allows ~20-30% thinner EOT (higher Cs) at the same leakage, and trims the dielectric-defect part of the leakage tail. Uses existing ALD tools.

title: Store the absence: deep-depletion SiC capacitors hold bits for years
idea: Reverse what the bit is: a 4H-SiC MOS capacitor pulsed into deep depletion stores '1' as a missing inversion layer; with a 3.26 eV gap, thermal generation is ~1e18 slower than silicon, so the empty state lasts years at room temperature. Built on 150 mm SiC power lines with 0.5-1 um steppers.
why: Refresh (fact 3) eliminated, U.S. manufacturability (SiC fabs exist domestically); ~1 um2 cells, so first market is refresh-free, hot or rad-hard memory tiers.

title: Ruthenium electrodes reclaimed as volatile RuO4 into ALD precursor
idea: TRIZ #38 Strong oxidants: specify Ru electrodes (which template rutile TiO2 with k~80-100) and design the recycling route in from day one. Ozone-treat shredded dies at ~100 C so Ru leaves as volatile RuO4, trap it in a cold scrubber and convert it directly back to Ru ALD precursor, closing the loop for a metal mined at only ~30 t/yr.
why: Fact 1 via high-k rutile, without the supply risk of a South-Africa-concentrated metal; near-total Ru recovery.

title: Thinfilm PVDF fixed: vapor-deposited aromatic polyurea ferroelectric
idea: Printed PVDF-TrFE FeRAM (Thinfilm, Opticom) died partly because its ~100-130 C Curie point and slow switching ruled out hot or fast use. Vapor-deposition-polymerize an aromatic polyurea whose urea dipoles lock into H-bonded sheets that stay polar above ~200 C, coating 3D trenches conformally at room temperature.
why: An organic nonvolatile layer stable at 125 C/10 y, deposited at room temperature for monolithic many-tier stacks, with no ALD or EUV for the storage layer.
